issue.body:
Can rebuilding after historical resets restore correct-revision code without per-task repairs? Follow-up to #28, initially scoped to MACS; investigation remains open.

**Candidate evidence:** an opt-in hook replays recorded bootstrap commands after patch application in native validation and exported verification. Twelve compiled lifecycle checks, seven graded-export checks and six complete native-validator checks pass. The native check produces the expected F2P/P2P sets; pre/post build failures stop validation. Default-off outcomes and commands match upstream.

**Integration:** the complete patched upstream package loads configuration, constructs the registered pipeline, builds tasks and writes Harbor files for default/on/off settings. Missing rebuild commands and unknown options are rejected. No external calls occur in these checks. This is synthetic local evidence, not biological recovery or a full generation CLI/Docker/Harbor run; the dependency environment is recorded and is not upstream's full locked environment.

**Current baseline comparison:** MACS PR792 remains the frozen earliest extension-removal pair. A recorded-command replay is submitted: all 16 original BASH inputs, including three syntax-error exits that upstream continued past, with no command/dependency repair or model calls. The saved Dockerfile stops on those errors. Reconstruction and biological validity remain unproven. [Replay protocol](https://github.com/Open-Athena/biotasks/blob/5f3c2945/experiments/31-historical-builds/macs-replay-protocol.md).

**Remaining:** establish a faithful executable baseline before the original/candidate MACS comparison. Correct-revision compilation in a fixture does not prove historical dependency compatibility or task suitability. Zero model calls. One reserved-CPU replay job is submitted, at most 8 allocated CPU-hours within a 16-hour first-stage ceiling. Any retained image is only for the pending PR792 comparison and must be cleaned up afterward. Research only, nothing promoted to main.

[Native outcomes](https://github.com/Open-Athena/biotasks/blob/6c03d407/experiments/31-historical-builds/native-outcome-results.json) · [Package integration](https://github.com/Open-Athena/biotasks/blob/6c03d407/experiments/31-historical-builds/package-integration-results.json) · [Frozen MACS case](https://github.com/Open-Athena/biotasks/blob/6c03d407/experiments/31-historical-builds/macs-case.json) · [Full scope](https://github.com/Open-Athena/biotasks/blob/6c03d407/experiments/31-historical-builds/issue-scope.md). Detailed logs remain in comments.

comment_body:
🤖 Submitted `biotasks31-macs-recorded-001` to establish a faithful baseline before the frozen MACS PR792 lifecycle comparison. [Checkpoint and protocol](https://github.com/Open-Athena/biotasks/blob/5f3c2945/experiments/31-historical-builds/macs-replay-protocol.md).

The saved Dockerfile stops at syntax errors that the original bootstrap agent continued past. Reuse the recorded-command method already exercised on Scanpy: replay all 16 original MACS BASH inputs byte-for-byte, including three expected exit-2 commands, in the original persistent Bash sandbox. Keep source-bound clone, full checkout copy and post-bootstrap smoke/git/fresh checks. Stop on any unexpected exit or timeout. No command, dependency, test or per-PR recipe repair; no model calls. The original smoke/fresh flags were false and are not relabeled.

This job does not apply the rebuild candidate or validate PR792. One existing reserved TRC worker, 4 allocated CPUs/16 GiB RAM/16 GiB disk, one attempt, 7,200-second total bound (8 CPU-hours maximum); each sandbox is 1.5 CPU/6 GiB with the original 300-second action limit. #31's first remote stage is capped at 16 allocated CPU-hours and $0 model spend, with zero prior remote usage. No new capacity. Only a completed replay image may be retained for the separately checkpointed PR792 comparison; all other owned resources are removed. The reconstruction result and archive readback remain pending.
